title: Male borrowers who specify a concrete loan amount in local currency may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the broader purpose or outcome of the loan rather than specific inventory needs fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention purchasing a smartphone for school learning may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a specific province in the Philippines may fund faster.
Explicitly asking lenders for help or pleading for funding predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who explicitly name the lending institution (NWTF) may fund more slowly.
Male borrowers who mention a loyal customer base fund faster.
Pitches from women that explicitly reference previous successful loan cycles with NWTF are associated with increased funding speed.
Male borrowers who mention specific institutional affiliations or training programs fund faster.
Female borrowers who describe themselves as a 'devoted mother' may fund more slowly.
Technical specificity regarding business inputs and goals predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about their children or spouse's employment fund faster.
